text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "registry/dedup.py already provides the duplicate-detection logic: `def find_duplicates(households: list[Household]) -> list[list[str]]` (line 39), which returns groups of household IDs that are duplicates. The tests import `find_duplicates`, `same_family`, and `soundex` from registry.dedup.", "file": "registry/dedup.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "Duplicate matching is phonetic, not exact: `soundex(\"Mohamed\") == soundex(\"Muhammad\")` per tests/test_registry.py, and `same_family(a, b)` is the pairwise test; test_duplicates_found_by_sound_and_birth_year shows duplicates are found by sound and birth year even when head names are spelled differently.", "file": "tests/test_registry.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "ID validity check exists and should be reused: `def is_valid_household_id(household_id: str) -> bool` in core/ids.py (lines 31-34). It requires the format `HH-` + 4 digits + 1 check digit, and validates the check digit via `household_check_digit(m.group(1)) == int(m.group(2))`.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "To mark a duplicate as merged, reuse `def set_status(household_id: str, status: str, *, merged_into: str | None = None) -> Household` in registry/register.py (lines 59-69). Valid statuses are only \"active\", \"inactive\", \"merged\"; it sets `h.status` and `h.merged_into`, saves via `save_households(households)`, and raises KeyError if the ID is unknown. It does not delete records.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "Loading: `def load_households(*, active_only: bool = False) -> list[Household]` in registry/register.py (lines 11-13) reads all households from the JSON store (key \"households\" in REGISTRY) and filters to `status == \"active\"` only when active_only=True. To find mistyped duplicates the script must load all records (active_only=False).", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "Merged records are excluded from active listings: test_set_status confirms that after `set_status(hid, \"merged\", merged_into=\"HH-10427\")`, the ID no longer appears in `{h.id for h in load_households(active_only=True)}` — so marking duplicates as \"merged\" satisfies 'exactly one active record per family' without deletion.", "file": "tests/test_registry.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "Registration-time guards exist but do not help the merge: `register_household` raises ValueError for a duplicate ID or an invalid region (e.g. \"ZZZ\"), and `next_household_id()` assigns the next sequential ID. These are for new registrations only; existing mistyped records must be fixed by the merge script.", "file": "tests/test_registry.py"}]}}
